title: QuickBooks Alternatives 2026: Prices and Plans Compared
h1: QuickBooks Alternatives 2026: Prices, Plans and Limits Compared
metaDescription: QuickBooks alternatives for small business accounting and invoicing: FreshBooks, Xero, Zoho Books, Wave and Zoho Invoice, with published prices, limits and cost examples.
intro:
What should I use instead of QuickBooks? The products most often compared are FreshBooks, Xero, Zoho Books, Wave and Zoho Invoice, and the right pick depends on how many people need a login, how many clients or invoices you bill, and whether your accountant needs to work in the same file. This page covers QuickBooks alternatives for small businesses and freelancers, using each company's published prices.

The subject is [QuickBooks](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/) Online, which Intuit sells in five tiers, from a free plan to a $340 a month Advanced plan. The alternatives price differently: FreshBooks by billable clients, Xero and Zoho Books by plan tier, and Wave by card-payment fees on its free plan. The page lists what each provider publishes. It is not financial, tax or accounting advice.

For context on the wider category, see our [roundup of accounting software for freelancers](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/) and the [side-by-side comparison hub](/compare/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a QuickBooks Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with the billing unit, because it decides how the price grows. QuickBooks charges by plan tier, and each tier caps the number of users: one on Simple Start, three on Essentials, five on Plus and 25 on Advanced. FreshBooks charges by billable clients, so a firm with few clients and many invoices pays little, while a firm with hundreds of small clients moves to the top plan. Xero and Zoho Books charge by tier, and Zoho Books also publishes user and invoice limits on every tier. Wave charges nothing for software on Starter and earns its fee from card payments.

Next, count the people who need a login. A two-person firm fits QuickBooks Essentials, Zoho Books Standard, or a FreshBooks plan plus a paid team-member seat. Check whether your bookkeeper or accountant is counted as a user or has a separate free seat, since QuickBooks lists two accountant seats on its lower plans and Zoho Books includes one accountant on its free plan.

Then check what the entry plan limits. Xero Early caps invoices and quotes at 20 and bills at 5. QuickBooks Free allows 2 invoices a month. Zoho Invoice allows 500 invoices a year. A cap that looks generous at 10 clients can bind at 100.

Finally, separate subscription prices from payment fees and add-ons. Card processing, Automated Clearing House (ACH) bank transfers, payroll and extra users are priced apart from the monthly plan. Wave payroll, FreshBooks payroll at $40 a month plus $6 per user, and Xero payroll at $36 a month plus $6 per person all sit on top of the plan.

A short checklist:

- How many people need to log in, and is the accountant counted?
- How many invoices, bills and clients do you handle in a busy month?
- Do you need inventory, project profitability or payroll, and what does each cost?
- What do card and bank payments cost on top of the plan?
- Can your accountant work in the product, or will they ask for an export?

Promotional prices last 3 or 4 months and then revert, so compare regular prices. For a longer view of the category, the [invoicing apps roundup](/roundup/best-invoicing-apps-for-freelancers/) lists more tools priced by the same units.

alternatives.heading: FreshBooks
alternatives.body:
FreshBooks is an invoicing-first accounting product. It publishes four plans: Lite at $23 a month for 5 billable clients, Plus at $43 for 50, Premium at $70 for unlimited clients, and Select, which is quote-based with no public price. Every plan lists unlimited invoices, expense tracking, estimates and recurring invoices. Plus adds proposals, retainers, receipt scanning, double-entry reports, bank reconciliation and accountant access. Premium adds project profitability and accounts payable. Team members cost $11 a month each, payroll is $40 a month plus $6 per user, and FreshBooks advertises 80% off for the first four months.

It fits freelancers and service firms with a modest client list, where billable clients are easy to count and invoicing is the main task.

Versus QuickBooks, FreshBooks' pricing page lists no inventory tracking and prices around clients rather than users, so a firm with many small customers can reach the top plan quickly. QuickBooks Plus lists inventory tracking and a five-user limit.

Worked example: a two-person consulting firm with 30 clients needs Plus at $43 a month, or $516 a year, plus one extra team member at $11 a month, or $132, for $648 a year at regular prices. The same firm on QuickBooks Essentials, which includes three users, pays $85 a month, or $1,020 a year.

alternatives.heading: Xero
alternatives.body:
Xero is an accounting platform sold in three US plans: Early at $27 a month, Growing at $59 and Established at $97. Early limits invoices and quotes to 20 and bills to 5, and lists bank reconciliation, sales tax, real-time reports, a 30-day cash flow forecast and free ACH bill payments. Growing lists no invoice or bill limit and adds a 60-day forecast, customizable dashboards and budgets. Established adds multiple currencies, project time and cost tracking, expense claims and a 180-day forecast. Xero advertises 80% off the first three months for new US customers.

It fits small businesses with several bank accounts to reconcile, firms that want forecasting, and businesses that invoice in more than one currency.

Versus QuickBooks, Xero's page does not list a user limit by plan, so confirm seat rules at sign-up. Its entry plan is tighter on document counts than QuickBooks Simple Start, and payroll is an add-on at $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor.

Worked example: a two-person firm that sends about 40 invoices a month needs Growing at $59 a month, or $708 a year at regular prices, since Early would cap at 20. Add payroll for one employee and the add-on is $42 a month, or $504 a year, bringing the total to $1,212.

alternatives.heading: Zoho Books
alternatives.body:
Zoho Books has the longest published ladder of the group. The Free plan covers one user plus one accountant and 1,000 invoices a year. Standard is $20 a month, or $15 billed annually, for 3 users and 5,000 invoices a year. Professional is $50 ($40 annually) for 5 users, and adds purchase orders, multi-currency, project profitability, retainers and inventory. Premium is $70 ($60), Elite $150 ($120) and Ultimate $275 ($240). Extra users cost $3 a month, or $2.50 billed annually. Higher limits are available by contacting the company.

It fits small businesses that want a free start and prefer to move up one step at a time as they add users, inventory or reporting.

Versus QuickBooks, Zoho Books lists lower prices at each step, but fewer small-business accountants may already work in it, which matters if you share files. QuickBooks Advanced lists 25 users, while Zoho Books tops out at 15 on Ultimate.

Worked example: a two-person firm on Standard pays $15 a month billed annually, or $180 a year, or $240 a year if billed monthly. If the firm needs inventory, Professional costs $40 a month annually, or $480 a year.

alternatives.heading: Wave
alternatives.body:
Wave's Starter plan costs $0 and lists unlimited invoices, estimates, bills and bookkeeping records, with online payments as an option. Card payments on Starter cost 2.9% + $0.60 per transaction, and American Express costs 3.4% + $0.60. Pro costs $19 a month or $190 a year and adds automatic bank-transaction import, unlimited receipt capture, late-payment reminders, branding controls and user roles. Payroll is an add-on listed from $25 a month or $40 a month, and Wave Advisors, a done-for-you bookkeeping service, starts at $149 a month.

It fits solo owners and very small businesses with straightforward books who want software at no subscription cost.

Versus QuickBooks, Wave's pricing page lists no inventory or project profitability features, and its income comes from payment fees. Check the current Pro card-fee terms before relying on them, since they differ from Starter.

Worked example: a two-person firm on Pro pays $190 a year. If it collects $60,000 a year by card on Starter, the fees are 2.9% of $60,000, or $1,740, plus $0.60 on each of, say, 600 payments, or $360, for $2,100 before any plan fee. Payment fees can outweigh the subscription difference, so the payment mix matters more than the plan price.

alternatives.heading: Free QuickBooks Alternatives: Zoho Invoice
alternatives.body:
Zoho Invoice is a free invoicing product, not a full accounting system. Its page lists limits of two users, three projects and 500 invoices a year, up to two organizations per account, and Zoho Invoice branding on invoices. It publishes no paid tier; businesses that outgrow it are pointed to support or to other Zoho products.

It fits freelancers who send a modest number of invoices, track a few projects, and keep their books elsewhere or with an accountant.

Versus QuickBooks, it has no general ledger focus and no paid upgrade path inside the product. QuickBooks Free allows 2 invoices a month, which is 24 a year, so Zoho Invoice's 500 a year is far higher for pure invoicing.

Worked example: a freelancer sending 15 invoices a month sends 180 a year, well inside the 500 cap, so the annual cost is $0. A firm sending 50 a month reaches 600 and passes the cap in the tenth month.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
This page is a price and limits list. It is not a fit for several kinds of reader.

- Businesses that need a recommendation for their own tax or filing situation. Prices and plan limits are public facts, but which tool suits a given entity type, state or filing status is a question for an accountant.
- Companies with complex payroll, multi-entity consolidation or heavy inventory across warehouses. Only the higher tiers cover these, and a pricing table cannot show how well each handles them. The [business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/) covers a different part of the stack.
- Readers who want a verdict on which product has the best software. These pages list published prices, not hands-on results.
- Businesses already in the middle of a tax year with a working setup. Moving mid-year means exporting history and re-mapping accounts, a cost no price table includes.

If you are a solo earner trying to understand what you will owe rather than which tool to buy, the [1099 tax calculator](/self-employment-tax/1099-tax-calculator/) is a better starting point.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer About QuickBooks Alternatives
alternatives.body:
The ranking of prices on this page can change when a provider changes a plan. A new plan tier, a change in user limits or an end to a free plan would change which product lists the lowest price for a given team size. Xero, FreshBooks and QuickBooks all run first-months promotions, so a longer promotion would lower the first-year cost without changing regular prices.

Five facts would change a pick for a given reader.

- A user count above the plan cap. QuickBooks Essentials includes three users and Plus five, so a sixth person moves a team to Advanced at $340 a month.
- A client count above 50, which moves FreshBooks from Plus to Premium.
- Card volume. Heavy card collection can make Wave's per-transaction fees the largest line, not the plan.
- An accountant who only works in one product, which can outweigh a price gap.
- A need for inventory, which QuickBooks lists on Plus and Zoho Books lists on Professional.

Prices on this page were checked on November 13, 2026 and should be confirmed at checkout. Tax treatment is outside this page; the [guide to setting aside money for taxes](/self-employment-tax/how-much-to-set-aside-for-taxes/) explains how self-employed earners estimate it.

stillBetterFit.heading: When QuickBooks Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
QuickBooks fits businesses whose accountant or bookkeeper already works in it, since sharing one file avoids exports and re-mapping. It also fits teams that need its higher tiers: Plus lists inventory tracking, project profitability and five users, and Advanced lists 25 users, custom user permissions, automated workflows and batch invoices.

It fits teams that prefer a ladder with no annual contract. Paid plans carry a 30-day free trial and can be canceled at any time. The cost is the price: Simple Start at $38 a month lists one user, and the regular price of Essentials is $85 a month. A solo owner who only sends invoices can pay far less with Wave, Zoho Books Free or Zoho Invoice.

A firm that already uses QuickBooks and pays an accountant to maintain it will often find the switch costs more than the saving, because data export, account mapping and retraining take paid time.

verdict: Each product above publishes its prices on its own site. QuickBooks lists the highest regular tier prices of the group, FreshBooks prices by client count, Xero and Zoho Books price by tier, and Wave, Zoho Books and Zoho Invoice publish free entry plans with limits. For QuickBooks alternatives, the next step is to count your users, clients and monthly invoices, then compare those numbers with the limits in the table.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: The most common QuickBooks alternatives are FreshBooks, Xero, Zoho Books, Wave and Zoho Invoice. FreshBooks suits client-based billing, Xero and Zoho Books are full accounting tools priced by tier, Wave pairs free software with payment fees, and Zoho Invoice covers invoicing only. Compare users, invoice limits and payment fees before the monthly price.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest QuickBooks alternative?
faqs.answer: Wave Starter ($0), Zoho Books Free and Zoho Invoice ($0) publish free plans with limits. Wave charges 2.9% + $0.60 per card payment, Zoho Books Free allows one user plus one accountant and 1,000 invoices a year, and Zoho Invoice allows 500 invoices a year. Free plans cap users, invoices or features.

faqs.question: Is there a free version of QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: QuickBooks Online lists a Free plan at $0 with one user, 2 invoices a month, one connected bank and its top three reports. Paid plans start at $38 a month for Simple Start.

faqs.question: Do the prices on this page include promotions?
faqs.answer: No. The table shows regular published prices. QuickBooks lists 50% off for three months, FreshBooks lists 80% off for four months and Xero lists 80% off for three months for new customers. Promotional prices revert to regular prices afterward.

faqs.question: Which QuickBooks alternative lets more than one person log in?
faqs.answer: Zoho Books Standard includes 3 users at $20 a month ($15 billed annually), and QuickBooks Essentials includes 3 users at $85 a month. FreshBooks sells team members at $11 a month each, and Xero does not list user limits by plan on its pricing page.

faqs.question: Does this page give accounting advice?
faqs.answer: No. It lists published prices and plan limits and is not financial, tax or accounting advice.
